## Purpose
`lapidation.rs` and `orient.rs` both project `.claude/grain.model.json` into a small, deterministic, byte-stable view handed to an agent's context window — a "convention map" and a "terrain census" respectively. Both are explicit about what they deliberately do NOT do (no prompt-word matching, no suggestion), citing measured field evidence for the restriction, and both fail open to an empty projection on a missing/unparseable model.

## Convention
Folder: apps/rt/src/commands/** · Extension: .rs · Files of this role in this subproject: 2
Both exemplars declare a `#[derive(Deserialize, Default)] #[serde(default)]` private struct mirroring only the slice of `grain.model.json` the module reads (never the full grain schema), so grain stays the single owner of the model format and every unread field is silently ignored. Size/recall constants (`MAX_ROLES`, `MIN_ROLE_COUNT`) are named at the top with a one-line rationale for the cutoff. Output is documented as sorted/deterministic with "no clock, no absolute path" explicitly called out.

## How to apply
A new grain-model projection command declares its own minimal `#[serde(default)]` read-view struct (never imports grain's internal types directly), documents any cutoff constants with rationale, and fails open to an empty result on a missing/unparseable model — matching both exemplars' "Fail-open like every projection here" contract.
